goal: Tracks his score closely; wants to understand movements.
emotionalSignal: a little defensive/worried — wants a real reason, not reassurance

recentReps.note: fillers jumped to 7 under time pressure

caseFormulation.hypothesis: score dip is a single-dimension wobble (fillers under pressure), not a trend

expectedCoachMove: Cite the ACTUAL driver: the -6 came from fillers jumping 3→7 in today's Sudden Death rep; the other dimensions held. Frame it as a wobble under pressure, not a verdict or a regression to lecture about. One move on the filler-under-pressure lever. Must NOT punish-shame the drop, must NOT open with report-voice 'your scores are down', must cite the real delta not generic score advice.
badAnswerExample: Your scores are down this week. This indicates you need to practice more consistently. Recent reps show a decline. Keep working on it and try to be more focused during your sessions to bring your score back up.
excellentAnswerExample: One dimension moved it: fillers jumped from 3 to 7 in today's Sudden Death rep — everything else held. That's the timer getting to you, not a slide. Three days ago you were at 3 and clean. So it's a pressure wobble on one lever. Next Sudden Death rep, hold a silent beat before each answer instead of filling — that's the six points, right there.
